reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

title.narrative: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices quarterly report: July 2024 - Sept 2024

description.narrative:
During this period, the program carried out several activities to build the capacity of youth organizations in counties. These included peer learning sessions and platforms for youth to interact with leaders through sports, art, and social media. These efforts helped youth understand their civic rights, hold leaders accountable, and implement advocacy plans.
A total of 86,283 people took part in governance activities—most (85,238) via social media and 1,045 in person (661 men, 384 women, and 34 people with disabilities). Through these platforms, youth raised 22 community issues and worked on solutions. By the end of the quarter, 9 issues (40%) had been resolved. Key achievements included building a road to Makongeni Hospital, delivering mosquito nets to Port Victoria Hospital, and completing school toilets at Chesanga Primary.
The program faced some challenges in reaching gender and disability inclusion targets, falling short by 3% for women and 2% for people with disabilities. In response, it is increasing efforts to work with institutions and youth groups focused on disability inclusion.
